notes.title: New economy world trial run
notes.content:
Over the past few months we've been working on a new economy world with a new map, new systems and different way of handling skills and progression. Vaguely set in the country lanes of 1930s England (except with ostriches), its the perfect place to give your tractor an outing this weekend.  

For the next couple of days we'll be running an open-trial of the world ; it would be great to see you there. Feedback, bug reports, suggestions or ideas would all be welcome.. or just come along and say Hi! :)

The world, for some reason, is called '[b]Babylon nTing[/b]' and you can get there through the finite drive in the cockpit in space. (i.e. The Usual Method for travelling to 1930s England).

More details of the world and economy design in the discussion thread.  Full release later in the year.

notes.title: Bugfix & minor update notes for Spring 2023
notes.content:
Here's an initial list of some of the minor fixes and updates that have been added to the game over the past few months.. 
[h2]New stuff[/h2]
[list]
[*][b]Loads of World Editor improvements[/b] : New Screens: GamePlay -> Player Start controls and Global Weapons Settings, Vehicle Setup, Weapons Setup. New layout to make it easier and clearer when you're assigning and uploading models & textures to a world. Lots of work on the asset browser and asset upload screens, including the asset scale and orientation control which means you can adjust per-instance model sizes without having to change the model file - very useful!.  Eraser options for removing walls, bg models etc (which now are reflected immediately on client), landscape editing - you can now paint terrain and have it uploaded to the server -,  better drag and drop controls for buildings, etc, etc. The World Editor is getting really quite useful now.
[*][b]New Weapon Systems[/b] : Lots of rearranging weapon settings - tieing in new per-vehicle weapon slots and making global settings like 'energy-damage-link' mode configurable, etc, etc
[*][b]Linux World Servers & cloud hosting[/b] - World servers now running on Linux again, along with new options to allow automated cloud hosting at the click of a button.
[*][b]Lots of Space Stuff[/b] - New galaxy map, tactical map, Orbit cam, Mining systems, Drives, Trade, tracking of star systems visited - all that kinda stuff. Also a whole new backend. Not finished, not particularly playable, but it exists again.
[*][b]Collision & Replication[/b] - The player replication and collision systems got a lot of attention which should make remote player positioning more accurate and reliable.
[*][b]Script improvements & trace functions[/b] - New scripted hiscores system, *scripttrace commands let you dig into what the serverside script is doing, and a whole pile of general script-language additions, some of which are listed below.
[*][b]Controller/SteamDeck Support[/b] - WIP but various parts of the game should now be playable with a controller. (needs a bit of effort on the controller configs)
[*][b]Various world limits increased[/b] - 60 vehicles instead of 24, 16 robocrow types instead of 8, 24 tiled surfaces instead of 12, 64 texmaps instead of 32, etc. etc.
[*][b]Model Converter updates[/b] - Better FBX support, thumbnail export, animation fixes, turret controls, ability to drag & drop atm and image files into the MC.
[/list]
[h2]BugFixes[/h2]
[list]
[*]Fixed pickup buildings
[*]Fix for spaceship textures not always appearing if ships were loaded before the DLC archive was mounted
[*]Fix for occasional crash if rapidly downloading and removing lots of assets
[*]Fix for not being able to lay new surfaces and texmaps in the world ed
[*]Debug tracking of render targets so we can easily track down a rogue one, Fixed some device reset issues that would cause errors when resizing (etc)
[*]Some fixes for reliability of the network connection.
[*]Fix for remote model selector screen just being a feckwit sometimes
[*]Vehicle setup screen shows that vehicle 1 graphic can not be added (and shows the correct texture in the preview window)
[*]Fix for asteroid graphics not loading if they appear in view before the DLC pack has been mounted
[*]Fix for weapon sys not being initialised on the client when theres no weapons.txt on the server
[*]Fix for shadows sometimes not displaying when in spec or RC
[*]Fix for profiler not always showing everything that was going on. (And related FPS improvements once we found out what was going on)
[*]Fixed an annoying little graphical flicker that sometimes happened when particles were about to expire
[*]Some fixes to the replication of turreted vehicles and weapons
[*]Fix for certain PC setups not being able to access secure URLs
[*]Fix for the static flags not showing blue when they're controlled by the opposing team
[*]Fix for *settings keyboard controls not working when in world editor
[/list]
[h2]Minor Changes[/h2]
[list]
[*]Changed the 'you can't go home when in a vehicle' logic to work off an Extras flag rather than being determined by the vehicle type
[*]Made the big yellow arrow above buildings respect the building's 'Dont show targeting popup' flag
[*]*savemap with no name now just triggers a save of the main map
[*]Moved the sun slightly to the south
[*]Added *buildingspecialevent mode 9 to temporarily hide a building (e.g. *buildingspecialevent [building_num] 9 [hide_for_seconds] )
[*]Added the movie camera on to the main/escape menu (Esc -> M) fix for weapons UI not being hidden when movie camera turns off the UI
[*]Added close 'x' button to top right of all world ed dialogs
[*]Improved dust effects and added settings controls for various colour and dust speed options
[*]When sea level is set to 0, dont draw the sea at all. (rather than pointlessly watching it z-fighting with the ground)
[*]You can now copy & paste text into the chat window & edit boxes! COPY AND PASTE! Whatever will they think of next :).
[*]Added osd text types for gold, silver and bronze text
[*]Added an optional extra parameter to *onscreentimer to include a text message that is displayed above the timer (i.e. *onscreentimer [playername],[mode],[seconds],[text_msg] )
[*]Spec Mode Limits = 1 means a player cannot access spectator mode unless they're in a safe zone
[*]Result of *renamebuilding command is now immediately reflected client-side
[*]Added *resetallstaticflags command to, um, reset all the static flag
[*]Safe zones are now recognised on the server so that the script 'am I in safe zone?' and delete safe zones commands can work
[*]Delete Building, Rename and Edit Message buttons in world ed now working
[*]Added mouseover tooltip showing current value for world-editor sliders
[*]Increased the amount of dynamic objects / particles that can be onscreen at any one time
[*]Improved the bullet <-> wall collision positioning
[*]Fairly major rewrite of the main server download system that should allow faster downloads, better compression and (hopefully) be more reliable and less likely to affect the behaviour of the rest of the game.
[*]Graphics -> Robocrow effects = 2 adds the mode 1 trails and thrust indicators to vehicles
[*]Unified the lighting calculations for the standard landscape and ground shaders
[/list]
[h2]World updates[/h2]
[list]
[*][b]Iridis[/b] : As well as making use of the new hiscore system and scripting up a fun little single-player challenge there (a proper challenge which is well worth a go if you've got any old-school gaming skills), I've added new features for controlling spectator mode and safe zones, new static flag graphics, a new energy bar display (incl. some programmer-pixel-art I'm quite pleased with :] ), improved particle effects, improved wall collisions and a bunch of stuff to improve the 'subspace' control mode that's used there.
[*][b]Lovelace[/b] : Have done a bit of rebalancing on this world, reducing a bit of the early stage grind and removing any remnants of the stuff that was pay-for (e.g. fishing is now an in-game-currency item). Still has its worth, but needs some more work to make it better balanced and improve the tail.
[*][b]Mechzone[/b] : Mechzone got a complete rebuild with new effects, new collision systems (mechs standing on buildings, you'd be amazed how much work is involved in doing that 'properly', probably worth it :] ), and a new design for a 'board-game' style mini-econ using an auction mechanic. Also needs finishing tho :)
[/list]

notes.title: Update notes for May 2023
notes.content:
Apologies for the brief delay (ok, 3 years. Fine. Be like that then).

A tractor v0.76.0 is now available. In this version:
- A new universe
- New worlds (mostly work-in-progress) ; Lovelace reset.
- Too much other stuff to list. (Ask a patron).

'Season X' has now officially started with a reset of all galactic players. If we're lucky I wont need to officially start it again before the weekend :] . Many things still need finishing, space stuff is limited but hopefully you'll have a few things to explore. Lots more to come over the next few months.

notes.title: Introducing Season X and.. the podcast!
notes.content:
[i](I'm calling this next phase of the game's existence 'Season X' just to suggest that its a defined phase we'll be going through.. it won't stay like this indefinitely.. There will be a reset at the end of it..  And I suppose its X because its, experimental? - But really just because i've completely lost track of what phase we're in :]  Anyway..)[/i]

[h2]Season X - Coming Spring 2023[/h2]
The main goal of this season is to support players to [b]build your own worlds[/b] (and explore those created by other players). Secondarily, there will be [b]space exploration & a galactic economy[/b], but in a slightly different (and more limited) form than previous. We'll also be building some 'staff' worlds and trying out new (and old) ideas there. 

[list]
[*]The 'season' should run at least 3 months, possibly longer.
[*]Anyone will be able to make worlds and make them publicly available in the galaxy if they wish. 
[*]Everyone will start in space (Initially. A new-player world may be added during the season)
[*]You'll need [i]Gal credits[/i] to buy autopilots, infimp, stardrives, space weapons, new ships etc
[*][i]Gal credits[/i] can be gained through:
[list]
[*][b]Playing on worlds & exchanging world wealth/kudos/etc at a planet’s starport[/b]. (Like the old galactic prestige system, different worlds will have different exchange rates and monthly exchange limits. i.e. Each world will have a different maximum number of credits you can earn there each month).
[*][b]Mining in space[/b]
[*](Possibly) By [b]attacking players who either are carrying mined materials or have a bounty[/b].[/list]
[*]Initially there'll be no space trade system, though something may get added later. (Last time we did space trade people used bots to gain wealth and im not sure its worth running it again for that reason.)
[*]There will be a few different 'staff worlds' to try, including an economy world that will be based on Lovelace but with some changes to balance & progression. It won't be quite so harsh. :)
[*]One or two 'staff worlds' will be for Patreon subscribers only. Patreon subscribers will also get a free infimp for the season (as well as joining the private discord and having to hear Fooli and I whittering on for ages about random nonsense in our podcast. Did i mention the [b]podcast[/b]?? :) [url=https://patreon.com/gamesformay]Check it out here[/url])
[/list]
At some point (probably :] ), Season X will end, we'll take the learnings from what happened during the season, the universe will be reset and we'll start again with something that will hopefully be a bit more structured and balanced.

[b]The game will remain closed for a while longer until we're ready to start this new season[/b]. It is unlikely to be ready to go before the end of April, probably later.  If you can't wait, subscribe to the [b][url=https://patreon.com/gamesformay]Patreon[/url][/b] and you'll be able to join the alpha universe and help test and build the work-in-progress version. 

With the game now being over 20 years old and having just spent the last 3 years closed - and with all the other things to do in the world - it'd be foolish to expect many people will want to play. 
But who knows.. if we make some good worlds and keep improving things, maybe we'll develop something that people might want to get into again.

Did I mention we have a [b][url=https://patreon.com/gamesformay]patreon page[/url][/b] now? :) Sign up to hear our podcast, join our private discord and all the other good stuff.

notes.title: December 2019 - Extended Downtime
notes.content:
As many will be aware, this game is basically a one-man effort and due to a range of circumstances I'm currently unable to support the game. This will result in the game and servers being unavailable for some time - I expect the basic service to be restored early in the new year.

More broadly, the game is not being actively developed at the moment and unfortunately remains largely abandoned. My sincere apologies to everyone who has invested time in the game and particularly to those who purchased items during early access. The game has always cost more to run than I've ever earned from it, and I will be modifying the steam setup so that purchasable items are removed from sale.

I do hope at some point I will be able to commit time to continuing development of the game and restoring the space travel and world creation elements, and it is my intention in the long-term to provide some form of compensation for those who backed the game in the early stages.

Apologies again for the poor service.
Mit

notes.title: Large ranch production rate bug
notes.content: Please note that the current production rate of cows at the 'Large Ranch' building is incorrect and will be modified within the next couple of days so that it is more in line with the other livestock farms.

notes.title: Auto logging and mining
notes.content:
To make the startup process a little less painful, the initial logging and mining sites both allow you to gain resources automatically until your inventory is full - just leave your tractor stationary once you've started the process.

Recent updates have also fixed some intermittent problems with the school buildings and reduced the negative effects of building damage.

notes.title: Building decay and death change
notes.content:
By the weekend all buildings (except special government-owned ones) will begin to decay over time, reducing their productivity and eventually disappearing from the world.  

Normal decay is very small and it'll take around 160 game-years for a building to completely decay, however the rate will increase significantly (10x) if it is not being used (i.e. Owner does not have the required skill to make the building function) and even more so (100x) if the building has no owner. (i.e When a player dies, any buildings they owned will disappear from the world after 3 or 4 real-time days if they are not purchased by someone else). 

You can pay to repair damaged buildings, the cost being proportional to the amount of decay to repair and the original cost of the building. 

Separately, there will be a change to the rules concerning death and stocks : When someone dies, all building stores and investment will be removed before the building is put up for sale.

notes.title: New worlds are tough
notes.content:
And this one is particularly hard going, what with the hunger and the thirst and the lack of anywhere to buy any decent food or drink. Poor uncivilized people are dropping like flies.

For that reason a charitable organisation has provided a small, one-off survival pack which can be claimed from the government offices, and if that doesn't work they may well be organising a live concert event in the near future, featuring U2 and a life-like replica of Sting if you're very unlucky.

notes.title: New world starts tonight
notes.content:
For those of you joining us on [b]Lovelace[/b], just a reminder that the new world is very much alpha-style 'Early Access'. I've had very little chance to test things (or indeed, to finish writing them :] ) and there's a fair chance that something will go terribly wrong in the first few hours or days. Its not unlikely that something breaks such that the world has to be restarted again not long after.

You'll also probably find life quite slow and difficult at the beginning (you are, after all, rebuilding civilization from scratch, and that's never an easy task), but with any luck not [i]everyone[/i] will immediately die of starvation :].

If you find any bugs, exploits or unbalanced production lines (etc etc), please drop a note on the discussion boards and I'll do my best to get it addressed as soon as I can. I will try to make sure any significant adjustments that might affect your business plans are announced in advance and as promptly as possible.

notes.title: Nutritional value and other changes
notes.content:
A few highlights from recent code updates :

[list]
[*] (Most notably) - New nutritional value system means that if you consume (eat or drink) the same item repeatedly its nutritional value goes down (down to half its maximum value) - e.g If you drink nothing but Tea all the time, you'll only be getting 50% thirst reduction from the Tea.  [b]So basically, its better for you to have a varied diet[/b].
[*] 'Disposable RC' item replaced with a separate button
[*] Holding shift now steps up in sheckles on various controls that previously didnt support that. (e.g. set sell price)
[*] Fix for the 'Leave screen' not showing the benefit of food/drink items that are in inventory
[*] Fix for player reverting to vehicle 1 instead of default vehicle if they sell the vehicle they're in
[*] Under construction building plots can now be sold
[*] Fix for camera speed sometimes snapping up to a faster speed when rotating
[/list]

notes.title: Replacement of Resident's Permit
notes.content:
In conjunction with the start of the new world, I will be making some changes to the benefits of in-game purchases. 

For now the game will remain free to play and the restrictions for players who have not purchased items will be significantly reduced. Please remember that purchasing store items helps fund the development of the game, which is written and maintained by a single developer with the help of volunteers.

[list]
[*] The Resident's Permit will be replaced by a seasonal membership. Those of you who have purchased a Resident's Permit therefore receive the membership benefits for the next year. 
[*] All trailers will be unified into a single item that provides 2x vehicle storage.
[*] Basic fishing equipment will be available for game currency (90d at the Fish Market). The purchasable, real-money 'Fishing Equipment' provides the extra benefit of an automated catch system.
[/list]

The specific benefits of having membership will vary over time, and will be more apparent when we venture into space and to other worlds.

For now, the membership benefits on Lovelace are:
[list]
[*] Non-members will be able to own/rent 4 production buildings and 2 houses/warehouses, members can have 6 and 10 respectively.
[*] Skill learn times for members will be 15% lower than for non-members
[*] Members can claim a Membership Startup Bonus pack, providing 5s plus some Bread, Tea, Steaks and Beer.
[/list]

Those of you who have purchased the trailer, fishing equipment or resident's permit prior to these changes can claim an exclusive decoration item, please contact me by PM to claim this. Finally, also please note that I have updated the game's EULA, which can be viewed  [url=https://store.steampowered.com/eula/779050_eula_0]here[/url].  Please do not continue to play the game if you do not accept the terms of the new EULA.

notes.title: Next world starts Nov 3rd at around 7pm GMT
notes.content:
[b]Our new world 'Lovelace' starts this Saturday[/b]. Everyone will start afresh (though, of course, you'll keep any items you've purchased through the Steam store). The world looks much the same but works significantly differently. Most notable changes :

[list]
[*] [b]Job system removed[/b] - base production buildings like Oil Drill produce at a flat rate cost as long as the building owner/tenant has the required skill
[*] [b]New skill system[/b] - differentiation between job and construction skills has been removed. e.g. 'Farmer' skill allows you to construct and run a farm, 'Baker' skill allows you to construct and run a bakery, etc.
[*] [b]Barter disabled[/b]
[*] [b]New startup layout[/b] - No welfare, start cash or purchasable government buildings, instead we have a Soup Kitchen (thanks Emmie for that idea) and the ability to task for logs and rocks to earn initial cash.
[*] [b]Skill learn times will increase the more you've learnt previously[/b]. (See the GFM forum thread for more info : http://gamesformay.com/forum/viewtopic.php?f=6&t=270 )
[*] [b]Hunger and thirst rates increased[/b] ; you need to eat and drink more frequently to stay alive.
[*] [b]Various price limits are now enforced[/b] - items cannot be bought/sold for less than their base price +1d or for more than 3x their base price. (Base price is calculated by the game based on the global production figures). **
[*] Once an item has been bought or sold, you can only adjust its price once every 24 hours. **
[*] Once an item has been given a sale or purchase price, you can't stop selling/purchasing it. **
[*] [b]Various new building types and adjustments to the production chains[/b] : e.g. Vineyard, rice paddy, poultry farm, stonemasons (converts stone to stone blocks used for construction). Workhouses removed. Production rates have generally been slowed down somewhat.
[*] Construction materials changed so that higher level buildings require more items (e.g. 'Lvl 1' buildings require Stone blocks & Wood rather than just stone, 'Lvl 3' require Concrete & Girders, rather than just girders).
[*] Two starter towns - one residential/commercial, one residential/industrial - new towns will be added by a straightforward silent auction rather than election. (The starter towns will be sold off by a similar method later in the cycle).
[/list]

(** All of these changes have particularly 'interesting' economic/gameplay implications that I'll be monitoring over the next few weeks - they may get 'adjusted'.)

[b]As this is a single-developer early access game, there has been little testing of the new setup yet[/b] ; things may need adjusting as it develops.
With a new world like this, it can generally go one of three ways :
1) Everything basically works fine and, bar a few minor adjustments, the world carries on running for as long as it can.
2) Some things need bigger changes - e.g. exploits/bugs fixed and compensation/penalties awarded - resulting in some players losing out and others gaining, but the world eventually settles down and it runs for as long as it can.
3) Things go terribly wrong and everything has to get reset not long after it starts.

Ideally we get option 1), but be aware of the alternatives so there are no surprises should anything go awry. There is also the outside possibility that the new setup is so unpleasant to everyone that we revert back to Grey, or something like it, but I hope that won't be necessary :]

I'l make some more announcements in the next few days covering some changes to the benefits of the purchased items and EULA.

Questions, suggestions, donations of whiskey, all welcome as always.

notes.title: World's End - October 30th
notes.content:
Due to a combination of factors, the current world will end at some point on October 30th. 

When this happens [b]the player with the most cash on hand will be crowned as Champion of Grey and will receive a free inter-planetary shuttle on the next world[/b] when/if the technology is invented there.

A new world, 'Lovelace', will start a few days after. This world will look similar but have a substantially different setup, particularly in terms of how the economy operates and how players can interact financially.

notes.title: Warehouses
notes.content:
Advance notice of a small change that'll be coming up shortly - Houses will only allow you to store food and drink.  There will be an additional range of new industrial 'Warehouse' building types that will allow you to store everything else.
Existing house stocks won't be affected (you'll be able to remove non-food or drink items but not be able to add new ones), and warehouses will count towards your house ownership limit not your production buildings limit.

notes.title: Meanwhile..
notes.content:
Patch notes for the last few client updates, up to and including 0.74.1.8 posted this morning:

- Improvements and fixes to the biplane / flight physics
- Fix for jitteriness when viewing other player's biplanes
- Fix for player list selection changing when other people join/leave
- Added a little 'for sale' sign next to buildings that are .. for sale :)
- Global export price variation calculation updated so that prices tend slightly more towards the mid-range for an item
- Fix for stockroom transfer list allowing over-stocking of some items, and occasionally allowing items to be lost
- Added confirmation screen for 'demolish building' option on under-construction buildings
- If you've got no job, dollar (well.. sheckle?) symbols show up above buildings that have employment available and that you've got the skill for.
- Simplified shader option
- Fix for 'sell to building' not always showing correct stock amounts for demanded items
- Optimised some of the building render pipeline, and fixed a bug that was causing buildings to flicker occasionally in busy areas of the world

Note that the changes to fix remote biplane replication may cause some people on older versions to appear to move a bit strangely occasionally. This'll clear up once their version is updated.

notes.title: Major changes comin' up..
notes.content:
Advanced notice of a few major changes to the way the game is structured that are planned for the near future..

The first will be a trial switchover to an 'active employment' system - whereby workers will no longer be attached passively to a particular building, and will instead need to actively work buildings to collect wages - More details on this will follow closer to the time, .

Within the next few weeks I'll be removing the separate purchase of the Residence Permit and bundling that in with an initial purchase price for the game. In the near term, those of you who have got the game for free will still be allowed in, and the building restrictions for free players will be relaxed slightly. Those who have already purchased a Permit will gain extra benefits. 

Thirdly, players who acquired government buildings during the startup phase will be served with 'Compulsory Purchase Orders', requiring the return of the building to government hands.

And finally, we'll be adding in some new rules regarding the manipulation of the economy through the creation of 'fake' player accounts. Please note that this is considered cheating and anyone found to be cheating in this way will risk removal from the main world and may be denied access to new worlds in the future..

notes.title: Fix for landscape download issues
notes.content:
A mis-configuration on one of the servers has now been resolved, meaning those of you getting stuck on the 'Downloading Landscape..' screen should now be able to log in.

Apologies for the inconvenience.

notes.title: Client update 0.74.1.3
notes.content:
Improvements and fixes in the recent Early Access client updates:

- Improved collision checks on buildings
- Extra info on building screens to indicate when a building is full
- Tenant is no longer removed from building when it is sold (Further additions to this system will be added later, including a notice-period for removing a tenant).
- A few rendering fixes (incl. reducing the over-bright crops in farm fields)
- Some fixes for auto-drive/right click.
- Fuel stations can now be built in residential areas.
- Fixes for construction of region-based buildings, such as the limestone quarry and ore mines.

Also added a couple of new decorative items to the store. (Headphones and Wizard's Hat).

notes.title: New Items: 0.74.1.0
notes.content:
New in the ingame Item Store in today's update :
- Fishing Equipment
- 3 new decorations (Personal Bongochimp, Balloons, Ostrich)
- Movie Camera
- Purple paintwork.

Client update also contains a few bugfixes and an extra option on ESC then O to adjust the nighttime brightness ; for those of you with setups that get a bit too dark at night.

notes.title: Minor updates: 0.74.0.9
notes.content:
Various little bugfixes and additions over the past couple of days:
- RCs should now show up if flying from home
- New racecourse - including improved Ostrich racing 
- Bugfixes for the prize awarding of BongoGames ; more prizes will be available now, including on races and hornball games
- Some fixes to prevent invalid transactions - e.g. trying to sell more than you are currently carrying to a building
- Fixes and tidyups to the Export and Workhouse screens

notes.title: Patch notes: 0.74.0.6
notes.content:
A couple more minor client & server updates since the last patch notes, various bugfixes and little additions:

- 'Exports' building owners can now change one of the items they trade in once every 24 hours.
- Some server fixes that may resolve some odd connection issues as reported on the discussions page
- Fixed crow spec camera height
- Fix for people sometimes getting stuck as an employee in workhouses
- Added in-game options screen (ESC then O) and defaulted to WASD controls
- Workhouse owners can now adjust the wage level they pay
- Shortened the mayoral election process by a gameyear.
- Employers can now select specific users to fire rather than just picking one at random.

notes.title: Patch notes: 0.74.0.4
notes.content:
Minor client update (0.74.0.4) released today addresses a couple of issues:

- Fix for the 'Purchased Items' screen not working if you have a lot of items
- When you're renting a building out you can now access the 'Building Admin' section to adjust sale price etc.

I also spent a lil while adding in a funky Bonogchimp Worship Meter (so funky it has to be capitalised) but thats for another time.. :]

notes.title: A tractor first Early Access release
notes.content:
Welcome all to the new version of A tractor. 

The initial public release went well enough, with lots more people arriving than I was expecting and absolutely *no* mad running about, getting very stressed, trying to keep the servers from frying. No. Absolutely none of that.

I've released a couple of minor client patches since then, just to fix a few graphical issues and to include a few missing downloads that were the cause of a few lag problems when things got busy last night.

For those of you who are staying around, we'll shortly be witnessing the morbidly fascinating process of the mass death of a large number of passing casuals, most likely not long before we all start wondering how we're going to survive without any Tea.

Lots more work to come, bugs to be fixed, systems to be added and with any luck the Descending Chimp will keep us all safe and secure in the shade of his Giant Bongos.
